title: Ghost-slab allocator with continuous-batcher reservations and GPU-resident compaction
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: GPU-resident KV cache fragmentation causes elevated P99 latencies and higher memory overhead under continuous-batching workloads. Small ephemeral allocations from batching and tokenized context slices create many tiny holes; full compaction is too expensive and causes latency spikes.

Proposal: Implement a ghost-slab allocator layered on top of the existing slab pool that maintains lightweight ghost entries for recently-freed KV slices, combined with a continuous-batcher aware reservation window. The system will: 1) assign per-model and per-tenant soft watermarks and quantile-based slack to reserve contiguous segments for imminent reuse, 2) use a bloom-assisted eviction hint to prefer eviction of cold ghost slots, and 3) perform GPU-resident compaction via staged peer-to-peer swaps (CUDA IPC + NCCL) to coalesce hot entries during low-latency slack periods.

Key design points: segmented ghost slabs (small, medium, large), access-heat decay to drive ghost retention, compact-on-stabilize background sweeps that are throttled by latency SLO signals, and a lightweight fragmentation score exposed to the Console. The allocator integrates with continuous-batcher by estimating forthcoming prefix lengths and reserving transient contiguous ranges to avoid scattering KV pairs across distant addresses.

Expected benefits: 15-30% reduction in fragmentation-related memory overhead, 10-20% P99 token latency improvement on mixed batch sizes, and smoother tail behavior during bursty traffic without end-to-end compaction pauses.
acceptance_criteria: Ghost-slab allocator implemented and feature-flagged behind runtime.ghost_slab=true
Continuous-batcher reservation honors per-model watermarks and reduces cross-slice scattering (measured by new scatter metric)
Background GPU-resident compaction executes without exceeding latency SLO bump threshold (defined in telemetry) in 95% of runs
End-to-end e2e benchmark shows >=10% P99 improvement on representative production workload trace
Console shows fragmentation_score and per-model reserved_slack metrics, with drift alerts configured
implementation_plan: Spike: microbench GPU peer-swap throughput using CUDA IPC and NCCL staging (2 weeks). Create benchmarks for copy cost vs kernel eviction cost.
Allocator: add ghost-slab metadata, segmented slab sizes, and bloom-assisted cold hint bitset (3 sprints).
Integrator: wire continuous-batcher reservations into request router so prefix estimates can reserve contiguous ranges pre-allocation (2 sprints).
Defrag: implement background compact-on-stabilize sweeps with adaptive throttle based on latency SLO signals and token throughput (2 sprints).
Telemetry: add fragmentation_score, scatter_ratio, reserved_slack per model; surface in Console and create alert runbook (1 sprint).
Rollout: gradual canary (10% traffic) -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with rollback gates on SLO degradation.
Postmortem and tuning: iterate on ghost retention half-life and bloom false-positive tuning based on canary telemetry.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Peer-to-peer compaction may violate tenant isolation if not properly bounded. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant compaction budgets and require ACL checks before CUDA IPC handles are shared.
Risk: Bloom filters misconfigured can force unnecessary evictions. Mitigation: conservative defaults and dynamic resizing based on observed false-positive rate.
Risk: Reservation windows may accidentally inflate memory usage under pathological batch prediction. Mitigation: quantile-based slack limits and global cluster backpressure signal.
Risk: Background compaction can impact tail latency. Mitigation: adaptive throttle tied to SLO signals and explicit canary rollout gates.
rollback_plan: Flip runtime.ghost_slab=false feature flag to revert allocator code path.
Evict ghost slab metadata and allow normal slab reuse; schedule immediate full GC sweep if memory pressure triggers.
Notify Console and runbook owners and revert canary deployment in Kubernetes.
telemetry_signals: scatter_ratio (fraction of KV entries that span >1 slab segment)
